_about: The shock diamond: the pickup a character carries, and the minion that dies to it.
Decoded from android_game.bin, ETHCallback_shock_diamond. Where the remake's own data
guesses differently it is carried beside as _remake_*_not_applied, as keys.json does.
SELECTED BY ENTITY NAME, NOT BY ROLE. entity_roles.json files shock_diamond.ent and
fire_diamond.ent both under `pickup`, and its own note says they are distinct
callbacks - which they are: the fire diamond turns projectiles into fireballs and sets
hasFireDiamond on its carrier, which PortalManager::computePortalFinalPos then reads to
move where a portal opens. Selecting on the role would hand that entity this one's
behaviour in the four chapter-3 levels that place one, and a fire diamond would start
killing minions it never touches in the original. So the name is the selector and both
names are written here rather than compiled in.
ONE range, used twice, exactly as a key has one. The init writes
squaredRange = scale(30)^2, and that same value is the test for being picked up and the
test for striking a minion.
THE PICKUP AND THE STRIKE ARE A FRAME APART. The callback branches on ownerID at the
top: below zero it runs the unowned arm, which polls for a carrier, writes ownerID and
then RETURNS - the arm ends in a jump straight to the function's exit. The payload that
strikes a minion lives only in the carried arm, which that same top-level branch reaches
on the NEXT frame. So a diamond taken in one frame cannot strike in it. A key is not
like this - it is picked up, trails and opens a keyhole all in one tick - and writing
the diamond to the key's shape is the mistake this note exists to prevent.

_note: range_px is the root of squaredRange. The remake gives each placement a
metadata/trigger_size of 28 x 24 and presumably takes a pickup on overlapping it; the
original polls a RADIUS of 30 px and never tests a box.
The carry numbers are the key's and are shared with it in Carry.hpp: the carried arm
of this callback is the key's instruction for instruction - alpha 0.1,
GetInt('ownerID'), ByIDChooser, a seekNeighbourEntity over the buckets around itself
with a global SeekEntity behind it, and the same scale(40) forceFollowUpPosition
leash. What differs is the range above, WHO may take one, and the payload.
Who may take one: the candidate loop tests isCharacter and skips anything else before
it ever measures a distance. A key's admits isCharacter OR isMinion. So a minion
cannot carry a shock diamond - it is what the diamond kills - and the port expresses
that by handing Diamonds only the player as a carrier, rather than by a flag.
The loop does NOT stop at the first character it accepts: it writes ownerID and keeps
iterating, so the original is last-match rather than first-match. Moot, and recorded
only so the shared Carry::Acquire's first-match is not read as a claim about this
callback: only a character can be a candidate here and there is exactly one.
The strike is first-match within the same 30 px. seekNeighbourEntity with
MinionChooser - which is one instruction, a bare isMinion - returns one entity from
the bucket walk, and unlike the owner seek there is no global fallback behind it.
Buckets are far larger than 30 px, so a level-wide first-match cannot differ.
The other mechanism under the same role, and it is NOT a change to where a portal
opens. Its init and its carry path are the shock diamond's byte for byte - the same
scale(30) pickup radius, the same scale(40) leash, the same followUp(60, 20) - so it
carries by the numbers in `shock` above and has none of its own.
WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES. The carry arm calls turnProjectilesIntoFireBalls every frame,
unconditionally, before the isDestroyed check. That walks GetEntityArray
('projectile.ent') calling burnProjectile on each, and burnProjectile is killProjectile
- a bare DeleteEntity - followed by addFireball along the projectile's own direction.
So while one is carried a portal shot is DELETED a frame after it leaves and replaced
by a fireball, and NO PORTAL IS EVER OPENED. Holding a fire diamond does not move your
portal; it takes portals away and gives you a ranged igniter instead.
THE 64 IS A GUARD, NOT A REACH, and reading it as reach is the trap this note exists
to close. PortalManager::computePortalFinalPos branches at instruction 38 on
GetUInt('hasFireDiamond') off the character and, when set, returns
origin + (destPos - origin) * scale(64) and jumps straight to the function's exit -
past GetClosestContact, past the anti-portal test, past the retry loop, and without
ever writing its hasFailed or preferedTeleportEntity out-params. That looks like a
64x range extension and is not one: addProjectile computes
dirVector = normalize(finalPos - casterPos), and normalize is scale-invariant, so the
64 cannot move the aim by a degree. Its ONLY effect is the other thing addProjectile
does with finalPos - SetFloat('squaredDistance', squaredDistance(finalPos, casterPos))
- which makes the projectile's stored range enormous so it cannot reach its destiny
and call insertPortal during the single frame it exists before the conversion kills
it. A guard against landing.
The port needs no guard. Game runs the conversion before Portals::Tick advances the
flight, so the shot cannot land first by ordering, and nothing is scaled by anything.
THE FLAG IS THE DIAMOND'S, NOT THE PLAYER'S. The carry arm does
SetUInt('hasFireDiamond', 1) on the character EVERY FRAME it is carried, and the
destroyed arm seeks a character and sets it to 0. So it is recomputed here every tick
rather than latched, and a diamond that goes down a drain takes the power with it.
Destroyed, it spawns extinguish_fire.ent, plays playFireExtinguishSound and deletes
itself before clearing the flag.
_fireball_note: addFireball and both fireball callbacks live in ETHCallback_carranca.angelscript: a
fire diamond's fireball IS a carranca's, the same fireball.ent, so the port reuses
Turrets::Fireball and turrets.json's 130 px/s and 16 x 16 rather than inventing a
second projectile. What differs is ONE PARAMETER.
killMainCharacter. A carranca passes it set; burnProjectile passes immediate 0. The
contact callback tests it first and RETURNS on a character when it is clear, so a
carranca's fireball kills the player and the one your own tap bought cannot touch
What a fireball does to what it hits, in the callback's own order: against a sensor or
a carranca it acts on exactly ONE name - shock_agent / shock_agent.ent - destroying
that ring and itself, and does nothing at all to any other sensor. Against a character
it addFlames and sets hp = 0, which killMainCharacter has already gated. Against
anything else it destroys itself, then burn()s it if isBurnable and explode()s it if
isExplosive. A minion is not isCharacter and carries neither flag, so fireballs do not
kill minions - that is the shock diamond's job, and the two diamonds do not overlap.
burn() sets `burned` and plays a sound; explode() sets the flag the bomb's own
callback reads on a LATER frame. The port sets both flags after Fire::Tick for that
reason, which is the one-tick split fire.json already keeps for chains.

_note: The drain, and the reason the fire levels are finishable. entity_roles.json files it
under `scenery_fx` as a 'decorative drip emitter'; its callback is ByNameChooser
('fire_diamond.ent') into seekNeighbourEntity over its own bucket, then scaledCollide,
then destroy() on the diamond. Destroying the diamond clears hasFireDiamond, so the
drain is how the player hands the fire back and gets portals again. That is a second
role-table misclassification of the kind enemy_killer was.
Its mouth is the node's own trigger_size at its trigger_offset - 10 x 51 offset (0, 46)
in level30b, 10 x 76 offset (0, 46) in level31b - a tall thin slot hanging BELOW the
sprite, not a box on the node. Trigger::FromNode reads it as every other trigger is
read. The original's scaledCollide is between two sized entities; a diamond has no body
in this port, so the test here is the diamond's point against that slot.
Three levels place one - level29b, level30b, level31b - and all three also place a fire
diamond. level30b puts the drain at (384, 182) directly under its diamond at (384, 134).
level28b places NO drain, which makes taking that diamond a one-way choice; the level
has to be finishable with fireballs alone or with the diamond left where it lies.

_census: shock_diamond.ent: 8 placements across 6 levels - level15b and level16b hold two each,
level17b, level19b, level26b and level29c one each.
fire_diamond.ent: 5 placements across 5 levels - level15c, level28b, level29b, level30b
11 levels hold a diamond and 9 of them currently start: level29c and level15c are in
chapter 4, where the no_gravity and darkest flags stop all but two levels starting. That
9 is the figure the inventory reports `pickup` inert in.
The role is now IN Roles::IsPorted. It was held out while only the shock diamond was
built, because IsPorted is per-role and cannot say 'served for one entity name and not
the other': admitting it then would have claimed the four fire-diamond levels that start
in order to claim the five shock ones. Both mechanisms are built now, so the objection
is spent and the role is admitted honestly.
Of those 9, eight have `pickup` as their LAST inert role and flip to playing. level31b
does not: it also places a boss_spawn, and Boss::Plays does not cover that one.
gutter_mouth.ent: 3 placements across 3 levels - level29b at (478, 316), level30b at
(384, 182) and level31b at (240, 146), one each. Every one of them is in a level that
also places a fire diamond, and none is anywhere else in the game.
_not_built: Presentation, in a renderer-free port. A carried diamond is set to alpha 0.1 - nearly
invisible, which is the whole visual of holding one. An unowned one calls
bounce(0.9, 0.9, 500), which is NOT physics: bounce lives in
ETHFramework/utilEntityEffect.angelscript and drives a blinkElapsedTime counter, so it
is the idle pulse an unowned diamond turns with, the analogue of the key's idle bob.
That is why a diamond is state with a position here rather than a body, as a key is.
The effect entities and their sounds: shock_diamond_pick.ent and
playShockDiamondPickSound on being taken, shock_death.ent at the minion and
shock_strike.ent at the midpoint between the two, angled along the line between them,
with playShockStrikeSound. And the two earthquakes, startEarthquake(15, 0) on the
pickup and startEarthquake(25, 100) on the strike.
One branch cannot be reached here at all, and is recorded rather than built: the
candidate loop deletes the DIAMOND outright when a character it is considering
shallLeave's - tested before any distance is measured, so it is not a range thing. In
this port a carrier that has ceased to be never appears in the list handed in, because
Game builds that list each tick from the player and the minions still standing. So the
branch has no equivalent, rather than being skipped.
THE FIRE DIAMOND'S OWN UNBUILT PIECES, said here rather than left to be noticed:
- burn_projectile.ent, spawned twice: once at the carrier when a fire diamond is
taken, and once at each converted shot. extinguish_fire.ent and
playFireExtinguishSound when the diamond dies. playBurnSound and the
startEarthquake(15, 0) on the pickup. All presentation.
- small_explosion.ent and startEarthquake(5, 0) when a fireball ends, and
playExplosionSound on contact. Turrets does not spawn these for a carranca's
fireball either, so this changes nothing that was not already so.
- ScaleParticleSystem, which addFireball applies only when fireballScale differs from
1. burnProjectile passes exactly 1, so a converted shot never scales and the branch
is dead for this caller.
- The fireball's own portal transit. fireball.ent carries teleportable 1 and the
original names it in PortalManager's teleport path, so a fireball goes through a
portal. Turrets.hpp already records that as its own step; a fire diamond cannot
reach it anyway, since holding one means there are no portals to go through.
- A fireball meeting a crate that a launcher threw, or the beholder. Only what Fire
already tracks - burnables and bombs - and the shock rings are tested here.
